questions.question: The sum of 11 numbers is 660. Find their average.
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Sum of 11 numbers = 660

**Formula used:**

Average of N numbers = sum of N numbers/N

**Calculation:**

Average of 11 numbers = sum of 11 numbers/11

⇒ 660/11 = 60

**∴ The correct answer is 60.**

questions.question: Rs. 30000 is lent at compound interest (compounded annually) for 3 years. If the rate of interest is 10 percent for the first year, 20 percent for the second year and 30 percent for the third year, then what will be the total compound interest?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Principal = Rs.30,000

Rate for the first year = 10%

Rate for the second year = 20%

Rate for the third year = 30%

**Formula used:**

Amount (A) = P × {1 + (R/100)} T

Compound Interest (C.I) = (A - P)

Where, P = principal ; R = rate ; T = time

**Calculation:**

Amount (A) = P × {1 + (R/100)}T

⇒ 30000 × {1 + (10/100)} × {1 + (20/100)} × {1 + (30/100)}

 

⇒ 30000 × {1 + (1/10)} × {1 + (1/5)} × {1 + (3/10)}

 

⇒ 30000 × (11/10) × (6/5) × (13/10)

 

⇒ 60 × 11 × 6 × 13 = Rs.51480

 

Compound Interest (C.I) = (A - P)

 

⇒ (51480 - 30000) = Rs.21480

 

**∴ The correct answer is Rs.21480.**

questions.question: Find the average speed of a boy if he walks 1/6th distance with a speed of 5 km/hr and rides a bike to cover the remaining distance at a speed of 25 km/hr. The total distance is 60 km.
questions.solution:
Given:

The average speed of a boy if he walks 1/6th distance with a speed of 5 km/hr and rides a bike to cover the remaining distance at a speed of 25 km/hr. 

The total distance is 60 km. 

Concept used:

The average speed = Total distance / Total time 

Calculation:

1/6th of the distance is

⇒ 60 × 1 / 6 = 10 km.

The time taken to travel this 10 km is 

⇒ 10 / 5 = 2 hr

The time taken to travel the remaining 60 - 10 = 50 km is 

⇒ 50 / 25 = 2hr

So, The average speed is

⇒ 60 / 4 = 15 km/hr

**∴ The correct option is 2**

questions.question: Rahul can complete his work in 7 days and Raj can complete the work in 4 days. How many total days will they take to complete the work together?
questions.solution:
Given:

Rahul and Raj can finish work in 7 and 4 days respectively.

Formula Used:

If A and B can together finish a work in t days and alone can finish the work in a and b days respectively,

Then, 1/a + 1/b = 1/t

Work = Time × Efficiency

Calculation:

Let the total days they take to complete the work together be t.

According to the formula above mentioned:

⇒ 1/7 + 1/4 = 1/t

⇒ 11/28 = 1/t

**⇒ t = 28/11 days**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__**The direct formula in such cases to calculate the total time = (a × b)/(a + b)

⇒ (7 × 4)/(7 + 4)

⇒ 28/11.

questions.question: The time in which a train 1800 m long, travelling at the speed of 30 kmph, will pass a signal pole is:
questions.solution:
**Given:- **

An 1800 m long train is running at the speed of 30 km/hr.

The train passes a signal pole near the railway line.

**Formula used:-**

1 km = 1000 m,

1 hr = 3,600 seconds (s)

Time = Distance/Speed

**Calculation:-**

Length of train = Distance covered in passing the pole = 1800 m

Speed of train = 30 km/hr

⇒ Speed of train = (30 × 1000)/(1 × 3,600) m/s

⇒ Speed of train = 25/3 m/s 

Time = Distance covered by train in passing the pole/Speed of train

⇒ 1800/(25/3) seconds

⇒ 216 seconds

**∴ The required answer is __216__.**

questions.question: By selling 50 items, a shopkeeper gains the selling price of 10 items. What is his gain percent?
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

When Profit = SP of x items, then CP (in terms of units) = Total items − x.

Profit = 10 units; Total items = 50 units.

⇒ CP = 50 − 10 = 40 units.

⇒ Gain % = (Profit ÷ CP) × 100 = (10 ÷ 40) × 100.

⇒ Gain % = 25%.

**∴ The correct answer is 25%.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Number of items sold = 50

Gain = Selling Price of 10 items

**Formula Used:**

Gain = Total Selling Price (SP) − Total Cost Price (CP)

Gain % = (Gain ÷ CP) × 100

 
 
 CP (40 units)
 Profit (10)
 

 Total SP (50 units)
 Profit % = (10 / 40) × 100

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let the Selling Price (SP) of 1 item be ₹1.

⇒ SP of 50 items = ₹50.

⇒ Gain = SP of 10 items = ₹10.

⇒ We know, CP = SP − Gain.

⇒ CP of 50 items = 50 − 10 = ₹40.

⇒ Gain % = (Gain ÷ CP) × 100.

⇒ Gain % = (10 ÷ 40) × 100.

⇒ Gain % = 25%.

**∴ The correct answer is 25%.**

**__Additional Information__**

Gain/Loss on Selling Price

If a shopkeeper loses the SP of x items by selling n items, then Loss % = [x ÷ (n + x)] × 100.

Gain/Loss on Cost Price

If a shopkeeper gains the CP of x items by selling n items, then Gain % = (x ÷ n) × 100.

Marked Price and Discount

Selling Price = Marked Price × (100 − Discount %) ÷ 100.

questions.question: Shopkeeper gave 30% discount on the article having marked price Rs. 3500. What will be the selling price of the article?
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

If a 30% discount is applied on the article, the selling price becomes (100% − 30%) = 70% of its marked price.

Selling Price = 70% of 3500

Selling Price = (70 ÷ 100) × 3500

Selling Price = 2450

**∴ The correct answer is Rs. 2450.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Marked Price (MP) = Rs. 3500

Discount percentage = 30%

**Formula Used:**

Discount Amount = MP × (Discount% ÷ 100)

Selling Price (SP) = MP − Discount Amount

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/53552b64e701833c85547a3db48e873dc375e72df6a70cc96f41f05ece3b6feb.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Discount Amount = 3500 × (30 ÷ 100)

⇒ Discount Amount = 3500 × 0.30

⇒ Discount Amount = 1050

⇒ SP = 3500 − 1050

⇒ SP = 2450

**∴ The correct answer is Rs. 2450.**

**__Additional Information__**

Base of Calculations

Profit and Loss are always calculated on the Cost Price (CP), whereas the Discount is exclusively calculated on the Marked Price (MP).

Successive Discounts

The single equivalent discount for two successive discounts a% and b% can be calculated using the direct formula: Equivalent Discount = [a + b − (a × b) ÷ 100]%.

Marking Up Goods

When goods are marked up above the Cost Price to provide a discount but still achieve a certain profit: MP = CP × (100 + Profit%) ÷ (100 − Discount%).

The failed student percentage = 100 - 87 = 13% of the appeared students

⇒ 3250 = 13Xover100
